headline: Acquisition-fueled revenue surge swings FIS back to profit
summary_short: FIS reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $3.377 billion (+29.1% y/y), fueled by the Total Issuing Solutions acquisition, and swung to GAAP net income of $231 million ($0.45 diluted EPS) from a year-ago loss, though both fell about 90% q/q on a non-recurring Worldpay gain booked in Q1.
summary_long: Revenue rose 29% y/y to $3.377B on the Total Issuing Solutions (TIS) acquisition, favorable mix, and cost savings; Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 193bp to 41.7%. Banking Solutions grew 44% on TIS; Capital Market Solutions grew 3.5%, with margin down 32bp on higher labor costs and expense timing. GAAP net income ($231M) and diluted EPS ($0.45) compare to a year-ago loss but fell about 90% q/q, since Q1 FY2026 included a non-recurring $2.2B non-cash gain on the Worldpay stake sale. Cash was $744M (-1.5% q/q); long-term debt rose to $16.9B on TIS financing. FIS raised full-year Adjusted EPS growth guidance to 7.0-8.5% but lowered its Pro Forma revenue/EBITDA growth outlook.
confidence_notes: REGENERATION: this run was executed in explicit force-regenerate mode per instruction, bypassing the Step-0 already-exists guard; no FIS_US_FY2026_Q2.json summary existed on disk prior to this run (resolver reported summaryExists=false), so there was nothing to literally overwrite, but all figures below were derived fresh from the resolver's SEC-verbatim shard KPIs and the primary EX-99.1 press release. Ledger note: the shard's FY2026 Q1 priors (net income $2,366M, diluted EPS $4.58/$4.59) were inflated by a $2,214M non-cash equity-method gain from FIS's January 9, 2026 sale of its non-controlling 45% Worldpay stake (release Note 6); Q2's ~90% q/q decline in net income and EPS reflects that gain not recurring, not an operating deterioration. Similarly, the year-ago Q2 FY2025 GAAP net loss (-$470M) included a $598M pretax equity-method loss tied to the (since-divested) Worldpay stake and a $108M contingent-consideration write-off tied to the pending sale agreement (release Note 4); neither recurred in Q2 FY2026, which is why net income and diluted EPS show 'NM' y/y deltas rather than a percentage. Debt caveat: the shard's long_term_debt_usd_m ($16,948M) reconciles to the release's 'Long-term debt, excluding current portion' ($15,432M) plus 'Current portion of long-term debt' ($1,516M); it excludes the separate 'Short-term borrowings' line ($4,226M, revolver/commercial paper), so the shard KPI alone understates the release's stated total debt outstanding of $21.2B. extendedMetrics populated in Step 3b from this same press release (capex, free cash flow, buybacks, adjusted EPS, next-quarter revenue/EPS guidance); no bank-style 'financials' sector metrics (NIM, CET1, efficiency ratio, charge-offs, deposits) were disclosed since FIS is a payments/fintech processor, not a depository institution.
